claims.text: Corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel is influenced by the formation and stability of a surface passive layer.
Q235 steel composition can affect passive-layer formation and stability.
Q235 steel microstructure can affect passive-layer formation and stability.
Environmental conditions can affect passive-layer formation and stability.
A passive layer forms through reaction of the Q235 steel surface with its environment.
The stability of the passive layer determines the corrosion resistance of Q235 steel.
High-temperature exposure can degrade the passive layer on Q235 steel.
An aggressive salt environment accelerates corrosion of Q235 steel.
The corrosion resistance of Q235 steel decreases as exposure temperature increases.
The corrosion resistance of Q235 steel decreases as exposure time increases.
The predicted loss of corrosion resistance is caused by degradation of the passive layer.
The proposed mechanism applies to Q235 steel in aggressive salt environments between 700 and 900 degrees Celsius.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention invoke both room- and high-temperature regimes, but the stated conditions and boundary are restricted to 700–900 °C, so no room-temperature applicability or comparison is defined.

The broad hypothesis allows retention of protection when the passive layer remains stable, yet the falsification rule treats a stable and intact layer after high-temperature exposure as falsifying the hypothesis rather than supporting its retention branch.
